question: Does shared optical-density grain in linear RGB remove BC0 chromatic speckles while adding visible film-like value to fixed AO6 colour?

candidate.derivation: fixed analytical match to about .012 encoded change near sRGB 0.5: .012 divided by the local encoded response to one optical-density unit
candidate.noise: unit-variance Gaussian minus sigma-1.2 Gaussian low pass
candidate.channel_contract: one shared density delta multiplies all three linear-RGB channels
candidate.bright_end_guard: per-pixel analytical scale from source max channel to linear 1.0
candidate.dark_end_guard: none required: positive transmittance multiplication cannot cross linear zero

visual_gate.selection: first nine sorted IDs fixed before render

branches.automatic_fail: close BC1 without visual review or parameter rescue
branches.visual_fail: retain the primitive only if mechanically useful; do not integrate
branches.visual_pass: freeze the winning fixed arm and confirm unchanged on a disjoint full-resolution population

forbidden: change density sigma, envelope, guard, halation or thresholds after render
claim measured film grain, stock response or calibration
use the effect result to reopen AO7 colour promotion
integrate a product default before independent confirmation
claim_ceiling: development-only explicit density-domain grain value audit on fixed AO6 outputs; not measured film structure, population preference, stock response, calibration or product promotion
